image_description: A tall, dark brown wooden bookcase stands against a white wall in a domestic setting. It features five visible shelves filled with books and decorative items. To the left is a window with lace curtains and a framed picture; to the right is a potted plant and part of a sofa. A chandelier hangs above.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rectangular furniture piece of considerable height, notably taller than wide.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The object is clearly a tall, vertical rectangular structure, significantly taller than it is wide, fitting the standard bookcase silhouette.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tall rectangular frame with horizontal divisions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bookcase has clear vertical sides and distinct horizontal shelves creating divisions.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bilateral symmetry with open front displaying books and objects.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The structure is symmetric in its frame construction, and the front is open, revealing contents on the shelves.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Multiple horizontal shelves spaced evenly from top to bottom.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There are 5 distinct shelves visible, spaced relatively evenly, holding books.
Adjustability is an internal mechanical feature not visually verifiable from this angle without seeing pin holes or brackets clearly, which are obscured by books/shadows.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Some models have glass doors on upper section.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This specific model does not have glass doors; the front is entirely open. The checkpoint describes a possibility ('some models'), but for this specific instance, the feature is absent.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Constructed from wood particleboard or metal with finished surface stained painted or laminated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture and sheen suggest a stained wood or laminate finish, consistent with typical bookcase materials.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Front open displaying books and objects on each shelf.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Books are clearly visible on all shelves, confirming the open-front design.
The surface appears finished (smooth/stained). While no obvious knobs/handles are present, the finish itself counts as a finished surface element.

artifact_observations.location: Bottom right corner of the bookcase base
artifact_observations.reasoning: The bottom right edge of the bookcase seems to merge slightly with the floor/shadow area, lacking a crisp geometric line compared to the left side. It looks slightly 'melted' or ill-defined.

The spines of the books on the top shelf show slight warping and inconsistent perspective alignment relative to the shelf edge, a common AI artifact where text/linear objects fail to maintain rigid geometry.
The chandelier at the top shows some blending of individual crystal elements, appearing slightly soft or fused rather than distinct sharp glass pieces.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is indeed a bookcase and not a similar shelving unit or cabinet, verifying class alignment.
To verify the 3D structural integrity of the bookcase, ensuring shelves are parallel and the object sits correctly on the floor without floating or merging.
To check for boundary bleeding between the dark bookcase and the white wall/floor, especially at the bottom corners where artifacts were suspected.
To assess overall image coherence, lighting consistency, and detect any subtle global artifacts like noise or unnatural blurring.

focus_areas: Structural integrity of the bookcase frame (straight lines, right angles)
Boundary sharpness between bookcase and background (wall/floor)
Geometric consistency of books on shelves (parallel spines, correct perspective)
Material texture realism (wood grain vs. plastic/smooth)
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the bottom corners of the bookcase for any signs of merging with the floor. Verify if the books on the shelves maintain consistent perspective and if their spines are logically aligned. Check if the chandelier's structure is physically plausible or if it exhibits melting/fusion artifacts.
